name: Wellcome Trust
why_them: Wellcome is the UK's largest charitable grantmaker. As of 30 September 2025 it had 2,723 active grants worth £7.3bn, and it has committed £16bn to research over the decade to 2032 ([funding data 2024](https://wellcome.org/research-funding/funding-portfolio/funding-data-2024), [Third Sector](https://www.thirdsector.co.uk/uks-largest-grantmaker-reports-2bn-rise-value-its-investment-portfolio/finance/article/1945006)). Its focus is health research, not youth STEM outreach. The only public-engagement scheme I found, Research Enrichment – Public Engagement, is closed. It last ran in May 2022, and it was open only to current Wellcome-funded researchers, not to charities ([Wellcome scheme page](https://wellcome.org/research-funding/schemes/research-enrichment-public-engagement)). I found no open grant scheme for the Nonprofit. The only education-related evidence is a 2018 joint round with the Education Endowment Foundation (EEF), which is older than 3 years and so weak ([Newcastle University blog](https://blogs.ncl.ac.uk/icmresearchfunding/2018/02)). Wellcome is high-capacity but a low-probability prospect, so the likeliest route is indirect, for example through a Wellcome-funded university researcher.
to_verify: Check wellcome.org for any current open schemes in education, youth or public engagement. I did not review the full scheme list, and my search results were mostly 2008-2018.
Check the 2024/25 annual report for current education or young-people priorities and charitable spend. I did not open it, and the 2024/25 spend figure was not found.
Confirm whether the Nonprofit could be a public-engagement partner to Wellcome-funded researchers
Check for a named Wellcome engagement or partnerships contact
Check whether Wellcome has made any education or youth grants in the last 3 years, for example on 360Giving GrantNav
